title: From the people building it to the ones who have to use it, AI is creating all types of anxiety
excerpt: Therapists in Silicon Valley are finding that AI in the workplace is leading to greater anxiety for tech workers.
content_html:
The hottest new spot for tech workers is their therapist's couch.

A combination of layoffs, AI, and massive paydays has Silicon Valley questioning … everything.

BI's Tracy Connor spoke to Silicon Valley therapists about how the people building the next great tech revolution are feeling pretty rattled.

Tech workers have always had plenty of complaints about their jobs — from the long hours to the industry's cutthroat nature. But now they're getting a front-row seat to the disruption their inventions can cause, which can manifest in colleagues getting the boot.

One therapist called it "complicity grief."

How quickly this is happening has only exacerbated the problem. As we covered in The Great Coding Reset series, new AI models released late last year changed what many in the industry believed was possible in just a few weeks.

Even those who've reached their professional peaks are struggling. The post-IPO glow doesn't last long when you realize chasing the dream was a way to mask bigger problems, Bay Area psychotherapist Annie Wright said.

"Work is the most socially acceptable addiction," Wright told Tracy.

AI's still giving the rest of us plenty to worry about.

A top concern for employees and their bosses is how to evaluate people's AI use, writes BI's Amanda Hoover.

AI leaderboards and tokenmaxxing have fallen out of favor, forcing companies to get creative when grading workers' AI usage.

A big reason is that, to put it mildly, no one knows what the hell they're doing.

A hypothetical AI directive might go a little something like this:

You definitely need to use AI. Just don't use it too much. We have a budget to consider. Unless it saves us a ton of money, which would be good. But we don't really know how to measure that either, so any help on that front would be great too.

The best evidence that everyone's figuring things out on the fly is what some executives told Amanda they value most: an employee who teaches their colleagues the best way to use AI.

Dan DeFrancesco

content_html_zh:
对于科技工作者来说，最热门的新地点是治疗师的沙发。

裁员、人工智能和巨额发薪日的结合让硅谷产生了质疑…… 一切。

BI 的特雷西·康纳 (Tracy Connor) 与硅谷治疗师讨论了构建下一次伟大技术革命的人们如何感到非常不安。

科技工作者一直对自己的工作有很多抱怨——从长时间的工作到该行业的残酷本质。 但现在他们正站在前排，目睹他们的发明可能造成的破坏，这可以通过同事被解雇来体现。

一位治疗师称之为“同谋悲伤”。

这种情况发生的速度之快只会加剧问题。 正如我们在“伟大的编码重置”系列中所介绍的那样，去年年底发布的新人工智能模型改变了业内许多人认为在短短几周内可能发生的事情。

即使那些已经达到职业巅峰的人也在挣扎。 湾区心理治疗师安妮·赖特 (Annie Wright) 表示，当你意识到追逐梦想是掩盖更大问题的一种方式时，首次公开募股后的光芒不会持续太久。

“工作是最能被社会接受的成瘾行为，”赖特告诉特雷西。

人工智能仍然给我们其他人带来很多担忧。

BI 的阿曼达·胡佛 (Amanda Hoover) 写道，员工及其老板最关心的是如何评估人们对人工智能的使用。

人工智能排行榜和代币最大化已经失宠，迫使公司在对员工的人工智能使用情况进行评分时发挥创意。

一个重要原因是，温和地说，没有人知道他们到底在做什么。

假设的人工智能指令可能是这样的：

你肯定需要使用人工智能。 只是不要使用太多。 我们有一个预算需要考虑。 除非它能为我们节省很多钱，否则那就太好了。 但我们也不知道如何衡量这一点，因此这方面的任何帮助也将非常有用。

一些高管告诉阿曼达，他们最看重的就是每个人都在即时解决问题的最佳证据：教同事如何使用人工智能的最佳方法的员工。
